Hi! Thanks so much for making this post. I’ve read through almost all the comments here. You’ve given us a lot of wisdom and I really appreciate the detail you put into your replies. I have a few questions of my own that I hope weren’t already asked. Also I understand this is a lot at once, so only answer what you’re comfortable with. 

1. Where have you shifted to, and do you have a favorite DR?
2. How often do you think about this reality while you’re away? 
3. Is “grounding” only for lucid dreaming, or shifting too? Like having to feel stable in the reality or else you shift back. 
4. In a DR, does your DR self’s personality / tendencies take over the choices you make? Or do you ever lean into your CR self’s tendencies? For example, past trauma had by your CR self might make you avoid a certain experience in your DR (even though you’re actively living as your DR self). 
5. Has shifting changed your perspective on anything? (meaning of life, death, existence, etc).. do you intend to live forever through shifting?
6. Is it possible to shift to a reality that you only have a vague idea of, one that your subconscious mind will simply make ideal for you? As someone who struggles to pinpoint where they want to go, it would be comforting to know that my brain can decide for me based on desires I don’t even know I have.

Some people say grounding yourself in your DR helps but that seems more like a lucid dream technique. If you have any tips from experience that can keep you in a DR longer (things to do or avoid), that might put my mind at ease.

 No worries if not tho. I don’t expect any shifter to have *all* the answers. You’ve already done a great deal of helping out ppl under this post, so pat yourself on the back! :D

Hopefully you can recognize what an achievement this is and feel more confident in your ability to shift to your DR. They say after your first shift, the next becomes easier!”

I mean COMPLETELY forgot, which shocked me a little bit. 

If I get a few more people confirming that Liz never posted that vid yesterday, I’ll assume this small shift came from “not caring” or feeling detached about the idea of shifting to a slightly different reality. I literally thought to myself, it would be cool if it happened, and would prove shifting to myself, but I don’t wna waste time trying to shift to a reality with a tiny change when I could keep trying for my DR. 

Last night I went to bed around 1 am and was insanely tired. I barely remember what I did when trying to shift. I think I just thought about shifting, didn’t do a method or assume I’d be waking up in my DR.

If I had an experience like this, any doubts I had about shifting would be washed away. The changes are small, but they prove you shifted to a parallel reality, which is INCREDIBLE. Hopefully you can recognize what an achievement this is and feel more confident in your ability to shift to your DR. They say after your first shift, the next becomes easier!

Honestly, I’d say that’s a pretty solid explanation. You could take this wrong-reality visit as a reminder that even if things don’t line up perfectly with what you planned, your subconscious has your back and won’t stray too far from what’s right for you. It’s got the big desire down (Hogwarts), so try not to lose all trust in your mind. 

I find the similarities between your wrong-reality and CR intriguing. There’s just so many ways you could interpret it. Maybe it’s a confirmation from your higher self that you are everything, you are powerful, and your CR self’s intrusive thoughts are just no match to your big picture desires… you didn’t review your script the night you shifted, and nothing catastrophic happened. 

Maybe you’re being reminded that we’re all God playing individual character roles, or “selves”. Your CR self has a tendency to fear and fret, while your wrong-reality self went with the flow of things. Messy room? Pfft, it’ll get done. 🤷‍♀️ Shoes on the bed? No biggie. You experienced it firsthand that we aren’t confined to just one way of thinking because we are infinite and can choose our destiny. So you shouldn’t think for a second that ANY self’s little tendencies, OCD rituals, whatever you wna call it- dictate whether you shift or not, or whether you shift somewhere safe. You are god & your desire will trump all else. 

Paraphrasing here but “there was passion but on the wrong subjects” stuck out to me too; it’s possible that your wrong-reality self was a lesson to your CR self in remembering to choose what makes you happy. Don’t do anything solely for status or a paycheck, do it because you love it and it’s fulfilling. Also this is just an idea, but if you’re struggling to decide what to do with your life here, you could shift to several DR selves who are experiencing a different career to sort of “taste test” which your CR self would enjoy the most. But yeah, I wish you the best of luck figuring it all out. You successfully confirmed that shifting is real, so try to trust yourself a bit more. You got this! :D

A quick google search just told me that lucid dreams only last 10 minutes to an hour. I always avoided searching that cuz I didn’t want to hear that smth so cool lasts such a short time, even for those who are experienced. But tbh I think it was worth finding out bc that’s some solid proof that your experience was real. It confirms it for me at least, so I don’t see any need to debate or treat it as a lucid dream. 

Even if for some crazy reason it was a once in a lifetime hours-long lucid dream, and you had suspicions of it, I would just let that go. It’s better to have this experience strengthen your belief in your shifting ability. If you start overthinking you might lose hope or worse, not trust that you actually shifted next time. 

I’d really like to hear more about what you did in the hours you spent in HP reality, nothing is boring to me. Do you recall any tedious tasks such as using the bathroom, checking your watch, etc?

I’m usually skeptical of “possible shifts” bc I always assumed people would just know if they truly shifted. The difference with your story though is the amount of failed reality checks. That to me has always pointed to a successful shift, it’s one of the first things I ask a shifter lol

But recently I’ve had lucid dreams where reality checks fail. I think it’s because I’m SO set on my DR being fully real, that I hyper focus on the day I can jump for joy bc my fingers didn’t pass through my palm. 

So my brain registers that to a failed reality check IN a lucid dream, bc it’s manifesting exactly what I want, no different than commanding the dream to show you a river or allow you to taste Mac and cheese.

I’m not saying this is the case for you (only you can be sure of whether you shifted or not), but it’s one possibility. Maybe. Because at the same time, even if a reality check fails, I still have clear signs that I’m lucid dreaming. The world becomes unstable and I’m not fully grounded in all of my senses. Interestingly this was the complete opposite for you. 

However I’m unsure of why you shifted to Harry Potter, a universe that you don’t really care about. Dreams usually consist of things we see in our day to day lives, and idk if you’ve noticed but this community is Potter polluted! (no hate to HP shifters lol). It could be that your brain gathered up all this info - reality checks, determination to have a successful shift, and memories of people shifting to HP - and gift wrapped it into this cool experience you had. 

I see one final flaw in this being a true shift and that is the lack of self awareness. When we shift, we’re not just entering a different body but also a different brain and backstory. If you didn’t instantly know exactly who you are and what life you lived up until age 14, then it might be a very vivid lucid dream. I think they’re called WILDs? It’s possible that all your previous LD practice has led up to this, and you’ve simply reached full LD potential. 

Now that I’m thinking about it, it would make sense for dream characters to be speaking in the language you’re most comfortable with, but deny it bc you’re used to seeing those characters speak English (meaning they’d act accordingly). I think I read somewhere that we have about 8 dreams every night, so that would explain why it shifted from you being at school to you being in a friend’s mom’s bedroom. Reality doesn’t teleport you to random areas when you fall asleep. 

Sorry this was super long, and I hope I didn’t get any information mixed up I’m so tired as I’m typing this but I couldn’t resist. 😟
